correctness.rationale: The proof first classifies maximal independent sets as Ferrers-corner sets. For a fixed corner set, the necessary-and-sufficient greedy-output condition is that every omitted vertex has an earlier selected neighbor. The omitted vertices split into a lower-left Ferrers block and an upper-right Ferrers block on disjoint priority variables, giving an exact product. In either block, conditioning on the earliest active vertex yields the recurrence for \(\Phi\); every recursive state is strictly smaller. A standalone exact-rational checker exhaustively matched support and probabilities for all 127 connected canonical chain degree sequences of total order at most eight across 2,754,350 permutations.

value.rationale: The full greedy-output law on chain graphs is mathematically natural because chain graphs are the canonical bipartite nested-neighborhood/Ferrers class and their maximal-independent-set support is already known to be small. The theorem turns that support into exact probabilities, yielding the complete size distribution and all moments, not a routine single-instance computation. The factorization and recurrence expose structural bias of the random greedy sampler and provide exact finite benchmarks for algorithms and random-sequential-adsorption calculations.
